text:
alex: Heads up — massive attach delays for batch jobs in us-west3-b right at 09:00 UTC. lots of pods stuck in ContainerCreating for ~30s+. suspect local nvme saturation.

maria: ugh. any node logs or short traces?

alex: dropping snippets from an affected host.

```
# iostat -x 1 2
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1600.0  4200.0  64000  560000     128.0     3.4  12.1    2.0    10.1   0.2  99.3
```

```
[ 4567.890123] scrubber-worker[8421]: starting scrub cycle on nvme0n1
[ 4567.891500] nvme0n1: writeback backlog exceeded, throttling
[ 4568.110200] kubelet: attach timeout waiting for ephemeral disk (plugin timeout)
```

```
kubectl describe pod batch-job-attach-yyy
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning AttachError  3m   kubelet            Attach timeout: iops spike on /var/lib/kubelet/plugins
```

chris: This lines up with the scrub-scheduler flip we rolled two nights ago (per-host dynamic windows). looks like scrub scheduling can line up poorly with bulk attach waves.

maria: short-term mitigation ideas?

chris: a few options:
- label the cohort with infra.janitor.pause=true for the peak window (pauses housekeeping scrubs but leaves critical janitors on)
- adjust scrub process nice/ioprio so scrub threads yield to attach flow
- transient scheduler hint: prefer nodes with label ephemeral-quiet=true during attaches

alex: i'll try labeling a small cohort (us-west3-b-cohort-7) and flip scrub ioprio down.

sre-ops-bot: [action] Applying label infra.janitor.pause=true to cohort us-west3-b-cohort-7

autoscaler-bot: [info] Attach-preferred policy applied: prefer_ephemeral_quiet=true for us-west3-b-cohort-7

maria: cost/impact note: pausing scrubs will extend scrub backlog and increase total scrub duration (more sustained IO over ~12-24h). but avoids immediate failed attaches that waste GPU allocation and customer latency. likely cheaper to pause during peaks.

chris: agree. medium-term we should make the scrub-scheduler back off when autoscaler reports planned bulk attaches. tie a forecast API between sched and autoscaler.

alex: done the cohort label at 1728610045; i've also lowered scrub processes to ioprio 6 on those hosts. monitoring attach success rate and nvme_util.

sre-ops-bot: [alert] nvme_util > 95% on cohort us-west3-b (rolling sample)

alex: quick metric blip: attach success jumped from 68% -> 96% in the first 2m after changes. leaving probe for 30m.

maria: collect nvme SMART and firmware version for at least 5 impacted hosts and open ops ticket if util remains high. command: `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1` and `nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme0n1`.

chris: also capture per-host scrub backlog size: `cat /var/lib/janitor/scrub/backlog` — helps estimate extra IO cost.

alex: will attach logs and smart dumps to TICKET-4521. tagging hw-team.

sre-ops-bot: [info] TICKET-4521 created by alex: "us-west3-b batch attach delays correlated with scrub IO saturation"

maria: followups: schedule RFC for scrub-scheduler + autoscaler integration, estimate cost delta for extended scrubs, and consider automatic ioprio lowering when attach wave detected.

alex: filing RFC and pinging sched-team + infra-ops. will update thread with postmortem summary after 24h monitoring. :thumbsup:
